issue.title: Add Advanced and Complete Stage Progression
issue.body: Fluent Mobile currently stops at Community Review; there is no way to move an item to Advanced or Complete without switching to web. This ticket extends the record screen with a straight linear progression through the remaining checks: Send to Linguist Check, Send to Theological Check, Send to Consultant Check, and Send to Complete, each appearing one at a time as the prior stage is confirmed done. This matches the existing Drafting and Peer Check pattern: only one stage-advancement button is ever on screen, and confirming it opens a bottom sheet before anything changes. ## Functional Requirements ### Stage Progression Buttons - Display exactly one stage-advancement button on the record screen at a time, named for its destination stage: Send to Linguist Check (from Community Review), Send to Theological Check (from Linguist Check), Send to Consultant Check (from Theological Check), Send to Complete (from Consultant Check). - Community Review, Linguist Check, Theological Check, and Consultant Check are always open with no assignee, so display the relevant button to any translator, not just a specific assignee. - Enforce a fixed linear order: Community Review, then Linguist Check, then Theological Check, then Consultant Check, then Complete. There is no way to skip a stage or move backward. - Once a stage is confirmed done, its button is replaced by the next stage's button; never show more than one stage-advancement button at once. - Sending to Complete is terminal; there is no further stage to advance to and no backward movement. ### Confirmation Sheet - Tapping a stage-advancement button opens a bottom sheet before any state change, matching the confirmation sheet used for Drafting and Peer Check advancement. - Title: the chapter/unit name. - Body: "This marks [chapter/unit] as ready for [destination stage]." - Buttons: Send (primary) and Cancel (secondary). - Tapping Send dismisses the sheet and advances the item to the next stage; tapping Cancel dismisses the sheet with no state change.

comments.body:
## Engineering write-up (Dev Ready)

Checked against **fluent-api `main` @ `07927c6`**.

### API — ready
`PATCH /chapter-assignments/{id}/submit` already advances the full chain:

`draft → peer_check → community_review → linguist_check → theological_check → consultant_check → complete`

Post-peer stages (`community_review` and later) are already open to any project member via `ChapterAssignmentPolicy` — no new endpoint required for linear Send buttons.

### Mobile work
- Extend `getStageAdvanceDestination` / visibility beyond Peer Check → Community Review (today capped in `stageAdvancement.ts` / #258).  
- One CTA at a time + existing confirm bottom sheet.  
- Map API status strings carefully: API uses `community_review`; local SQLite often aliases `community_check`. Add destinations for Linguist / Theological / Consultant / Complete labels per AC.  
- Badge UI still collapses some advanced statuses — button labels should use the product stage names, not only the coarse badge bucket.

### Soft dep
#257 (offline stage-advance queue) is still open; online best-effort submit matches the existing #258 pattern until #257 lands.

Moving to **Dev Ready**.

**Test Results:#443**

- User can move the chapter from Community Review → Linguist Check.
- User can move the chapter from Linguist Check → Theological Check.
- User can move the chapter from Theological Check → Consultant Check.
- User can move the chapter from Consultant Check → Complete.
- Only the next stage-advancement button is displayed at each stage; users cannot skip or move backward.
- Confirmation sheet appears before stage advancement, and Send advances the chapter while Cancel leaves the stage unchanged.

**Issues Identified:**

- If there is no recording, the user is still able to move the chapter to the next stage. A new issue has been created for this: #542.
- When sending the chapter to the next stage, a confirmation message appears, and clicking Send successfully advances the chapter. However, this confirmation step is not currently implemented on the web. Could you please confirm if this is a required feature for the mobile as well?
Yes, the mobile does have a confirmation message and this is different from web. It is intended. This one can be moved to Passed QA. :white_check_mark:
